A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WAFT research. Their text, equations, four figures, six tables, and Appendix A are readable and support comparison, including matching the original model to v2's renamed a1 variant.

before.justification: V1 reports original optical-flow benchmark results, zero-shot evaluations, memory measurements, component ablations, and appendix sequence-level results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and reports additional encoder variants, memory measurements, and Sintel sequence analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains v1's frozen DAv2 plus ResNet18 encoder as adaptation a1, but introduces a2: only the backbone is frozen, the DPT head becomes trainable, and features are side-tuned with three ResNet blocks. This substantially changes a key component and supports Twins, DAv2, and DINOv3 backbones. Recurrent warping, five updates, and the MoL loss remain.

E1.justification: Section 5 retains the same seven optical-flow training datasets and evaluation on Sintel, KITTI, and Spring. The additional pretrained backbones are model configurations; excluding Ambush 1 is a subset analysis within existing Sintel coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 2–4 remain unchanged. Table 1 adds FlowFormer and CCMR+ to the memory comparison, while Appendix Table 6 adds SAMFlow to the sequence-level comparison. These methods already appeared elsewhere in v1.

E3.justification: The principal training schedules, splits, metrics, and iteration counts remain unchanged. V2 adds three a2/backbone configurations, profiles WAFT-Twins-a2 at 1/8, 1/4, and 1/2 resolution, and introduces an additional Sintel aggregate excluding Ambush 1. These extend the existing evaluation design.

E4.justification: Table 5's component ablations are retained unchanged. Appendix A adds a sensitivity analysis showing how excluding Ambush 1 affects average Sintel errors and the comparison with FlowFormer++; v1 already reported sequence errors but lacked this exclusion analysis. Table 1 also extends the memory-resolution analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. Parentheses in Table 6 denote clean-pass EPE alongside final-pass EPE, not uncertainty. The added sequence-exclusion average is a sensitivity analysis.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 retain a1 scores and add substantial a2 result series. For example, DINOv3-a2 reports Sintel Clean EPE 0.94 versus retained a1's 1.09; zero-shot KITTI Fl-all is 9.9 for Twins-a2 and 12.9 for DINOv3-a2 versus a1's 10.3. These compare different configurations, not reruns of an unchanged model. Tables 1 and 6 replace the focal a1 results with Twins-a2 measurements and add further result entries.

T1.justification: The full and partial cost-volume definitions, warping equation, and mathematical reasoning in Section 3 remain unchanged. Neither version adds original theorems or proofs; the new encoder adaptation does not revise the formal framework.

C1.justification: The central claims about simple, efficient optical flow without cost volumes remain. V2 extends the abstract's first-place benchmark claim to Sintel, supported specifically on Clean in Table 2, and the introduction adds explicit competitiveness with an ImageNet-pretrained Twins backbone. The best zero-shot KITTI and up-to-4.1-times-faster claims persist.

C2.justification: V1 emphasizes the importance of DAv2 features and ResNet refinement. V2 broadens this interpretation to pretraining and adaptation quality, arguing that strong performance does not depend solely on advanced backbones. Section 5.3 and Appendix A newly explain Sintel Final performance through Ambush 1 sensitivity and condition the advantage over FlowFormer++ on excluding that sequence.

D1.justification: V2 documents a2's freezing rules, trainable head, residual blocks, backbone sizes, and pretraining sources. However, it removes v1's explicit a1 feature-image concatenation, full-resolution head-feature selection, and three-deconvolution-layer description. The WAFT code/weights access statement and principal hardware and hyperparameter disclosures remain; the SPyNet implementation reference is removed.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Twins and DINOv3 references and removes Niklaus's SPyNet reimplementation reference. Positioning against FlowFormer and FlowFormer++ now emphasizes comparisons using an ImageNet-pretrained Twins backbone. The main related-work taxonomy and argument about reviving warping remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 introduces a1/a2 variant terminology, rewrites the encoder and several performance paragraphs, and expands the appendix explanation. It removes the brief conclusion and switches to author-year citations. Most prose and the main Introduction–Related Work–Background–Method–Experiments organization remain.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reformats the document through changed title/author placement, heading styles, header rules, smaller figures, and redistributed tables and text. Tables 1–4 gain rows, and Table 6 gains a SAMFlow column and an exclusion-average row. Table 3 now precedes Table 2, while Table 6 is separated from Appendix A by references. The four figures retain their underlying visual content.

improvement.justification: The a2 design and additional backbone evaluations strengthen evidence for WAFT's flexibility and reduce dependence on v1's mainly DAv2-based comparisons. Appendix A also quantifies sensitivity to Ambush 1. These useful gains are tempered by lost a1 implementation details and an apparent reporting error: Table 6 lists SAMFlow's average as 0.995 (2.080) under final-EPE (clean-EPE), reversing the metric order indicated by Table 2.
